newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to reopen talks with Alcoa on Inespal.
newsitem.headline: Spain to reopen talks with Alcoa on Inespal.

text.p: Spain's Industry Ministry will reopen talks this week with US group Alcoa on the possible sale of Spanish aluminium producer Inespal, local press reported on Monday.
Financial daily Gacetas de los Negocios reported that the US group was interested in buying Inespal, part of state holding company SEPI, in its entirity.
Nobody at the Industry Ministry was available to comment.
Spain's talks with Alcoa began some months ago, but were blocked as the companies awaited the signing of an electricity protocol guaranteeing stable tariffs for Inespal until the year 2001.
This factor was key as Inespal is one of the principal consumers of electricity in the country.
The paper added that if Spain did not reach a deal with Alcoa, it would consider talks with other foreign groups.
Among those tipped to be interested include Canada's Alcan, Dutch group Hoogovens NV, Norway's Hydro Aluminium and Swiss group Glencore.
In 1995 Inespal's gross profit rose to 15.67 billion pesetas. Its 1996 gross profit is expected to be around 4 billion pesetas.
